name: Maulana Junayed Al Habib
contribution: As senior vice-president of Jamiat-e-Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, he was selected for Brahmanbaria-2 through the BNP-led alliance's seat-sharing arrangement in the 12 February 2026 parliamentary election. He contested on Jamiat's date-palm symbol against independent candidate Rumeen Farhana.
context: Brahmanbaria-2 covers the Sarail and Ashuganj upazilas and was one of the constituencies where an alliance-backed religious-party candidate faced a prominent independent former BNP figure. The contest made local candidate selection and alliance coordination visible within the wider 2026 parliamentary transition.
impact: Junayed Al Habib's candidacy shows how the 2026 election translated national alliance agreements into constituency-level competition. He did not win the seat: Rumeen Farhana was reported elected, while his campaign remained a notable example of Jamiat's participation in the BNP-led electoral arrangement.
highlight: Jamiat leader who contested Brahmanbaria-2 through the BNP-led alliance in the 2026 election.

shortAnswer: Maulana Junayed Al Habib is a senior Jamiat-e-Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh leader who contested Brahmanbaria-2 through the BNP-led alliance in the 2026 election.

faq.question: Which constituency did Junayed Al Habib contest in 2026?
faq.answer: He contested Brahmanbaria-2, covering Sarail and Ashuganj, as Jamiat-e-Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh's candidate in the BNP-led alliance arrangement.

faq.question: Did Junayed Al Habib win Brahmanbaria-2?
faq.answer: No. He contested against independent candidate Rumeen Farhana, who was reported elected from Brahmanbaria-2.
